previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of recurrent abdominal pain and multiple prior hospitalizations was admitted for epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and inability to tolerate oral intake. Labs showed only a mildly elevated lipase (111), and imaging revealed a normal ultrasound with no biliary or pancreatic abnormalities. The GI team found no evidence of acute pancreatitis or structural cause, and questioned the validity of prior sphincter of Oddi dysfunction diagnoses. The hospital course focused on symptom management with IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics, followed by gradual advancement to oral intake. A motility bowel disorder was considered the likely cause of her episodic pain, possibly related to chronic narcotic use. She declined chronic pain referral but tolerated a regular diet before discharge. She was discharged home with instructions to continue ranitidine, Miralax, and home psychiatric medications, with follow-up for a planned outpatient ERCP and encouragement to consider non-pharmacologic pain management strategies.

    The scout film was normal.
    The bile duct was deeply cannulated with the sphincterotome.

    No filling defects were identified in the CBD.
    Opacification of the gallbladder was incomplete.
    The left and right hepatic ducts and all intrahepatic 
branches were normal.

previous ampullary dilations, a biliary sphincteroplasty was 
made with a 6mm Hurricane balloon.
    There was no post-sphincteroplasty bleeding.
    The biliary tree was swept with a 8.5 mm balloon starting at 
the bifurcation. No stones or sludge were removed.
    The CBD and CHD were swept repeatedly.
    The final occlusion cholangiogram showed no evidence of 
filling defects in the CBD.
    Excellent bile and contrast drainage was seen 
fluoroscopically and endoscopically through a wide open biliary 
orifice.
